cards.title: Balanced thought record
cards.summary: Separate situation, automatic thought, emotion, evidence, and a more balanced interpretation.
cards.when_to_use: When a distressing thought is driving emotion or avoidance.
steps: Name the situation in observable terms.
Write the automatic thought.
Identify emotions and intensity if useful.
List evidence for and against the thought.
Write a balanced alternative that is believable, not artificially positive.
Choose one small action.
cautions: Do not use this to debate trauma, discrimination, abuse, or real danger out of existence.

cards.title: Behavioral activation, tiny version
cards.summary: Use small planned activity to reconnect with care, mastery, pleasure, or values.
cards.when_to_use: Low mood, withdrawal, loss of routine, or task paralysis.
steps: Pick one category: care, connection, mastery, pleasure, or values.
Shrink the activity until it is startable.
Choose a cue and time.
Do the minimum version.
Notice effects without requiring immediate mood improvement.
cautions: Screen for safety and severe physical limitations before activity coaching.

cards.title: Structured problem solving
cards.summary: Convert a broad problem into a bounded next decision.
cards.when_to_use: When rumination is high but some part of the problem is actionable.
steps: Define the problem in one sentence.
Separate controllable and uncontrollable parts.
Generate several options before judging them.
Choose one workable next step.
Set a review point.

cards.title: Worry container
cards.summary: Capture worry and defer non-actionable rumination to a planned review period.
cards.when_to_use: Persistent repetitive worry that interrupts the day.
steps: Write the worry down.
Ask whether any action is possible now.
If actionable, choose one action.
If not, assign a review period.
Return to the present task using an external cue.
cautions: Do not defer urgent safety or medical concerns.

cards.title: Behavioral experiment
cards.summary: Test a prediction with a small, safe observation rather than arguing abstractly.
cards.when_to_use: When a belief makes a testable prediction and a safe experiment is available.
steps: Write the prediction.
Define what would count as evidence.
Design the smallest safe test.
Run it without stacking the deck.
Compare prediction with result.
Update the belief modestly.
cautions: Do not use risky exposure or experiments involving abuse, medical danger, illegal acts, or unsafe substances.

cards.title: Graded exposure planning
cards.summary: Build a gradual, consent-based approach to feared but objectively safe situations.
cards.when_to_use: Avoidance is maintaining anxiety and the target is genuinely safe.
steps: Confirm the target is safe and appropriate.
Create a hierarchy from easier to harder.
Choose a manageable step.
Stay long enough to learn rather than to force distress to zero.
Repeat and review learning before increasing difficulty.
cautions: Not for situations involving actual danger, active abuse, medical instability, or trauma processing without appropriate support.
